correctness.rationale: With the diagonal intersection as origin and unit diagonal directions \(u,v\), direct polygon-centroid algebra gives \(CM=(pu+qv)/3\) for \(p=\alpha-\gamma\), \(q=\beta-\delta\). The quadrilateral CCM lies on both diagonal perpendicular bisectors, hence has scalar products \(p/2\) and \(q/2\). Equality is therefore exactly \(p=2qt\), \(q=2pt\), whose complete solution is \(p=q=0\) or \(4t^2=1\) with \(q=2tp\). The explicit non-parallelogram witness satisfies these equations and has unequal side lengths.

final_claim: For a strictly convex quadrilateral with diagonal half-distances \(\alpha,\gamma,\beta,\delta\) and \(t=\cos\theta\), \(CCM=CM\) exactly when either both diagonals bisect each other, or \(4t^2=1\) and \(\beta-\delta=2t(\alpha-\gamma)\); equivalently, every non-parallelogram collapse lies in the stated \(60^\circ\)-diagonal family.
